name: Orthodox Marxism
summary: Orthodox Marxism is the systematized Marxism of the Second International, chiefly Karl Kautsky's, which treats historical materialism as a science showing that capitalism will fall through its internal contradictions and give way to socialism. It pursues this through an independent mass workers' party that uses unions, universal suffrage and parliament, holds that history cannot be hurried, and rejects both Bernstein's revisionism and, in Kautsky's later writing, Bolshevik dictatorship.
scope: The Second International orthodoxy of Kautsky (the Erfurt Program commentary of 1892 and The Dictatorship of the Proletariat, 1918), Plekhanov and the pre-1914 SPD, and Lukacs's definition of orthodoxy as method. It excludes Leninism, Stalinism, Maoism, Western Marxism and impossibilist or anti-revisionist offshoots; statements on modern issues are mostly inferred at low confidence.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not a Second International program item as such, but Erfurt-style social democracy backed social reform and labor legislation; inferred support for public health provision as a reform that eases workers' lot.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Kautsky counts labor legislation as the one useful philanthropy-type measure and backs union wage struggles, but warns reforms do not remove capitalism's contradictions; a wage floor is inferred as welcome but minor.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Kautsky argues production for sale must give way to production for use and that commodity production's contradictions grow; markets are the problem, not the solution.

public-ownership.rationale: The commentary states the aim as abolishing private ownership of the means of production and replacing production for sale with production by and for society.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Taxation of capital was an accepted social-democratic demand but Kautsky says reforms preserving private property are largely inoperative; support is real yet subordinate to expropriation.

unions-good.rationale: Kautsky calls the union movement the core of the militant proletariat and a school of organization and discipline, though he criticizes craft aristocracy.

property-fundamental.rationale: The program aims at abolishing private property in the means of production, so treating it as an inviolable right is rejected.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Kautsky sees trusts and syndicates as stages toward socialization rather than something to regulate back into competition; tighter regulation is accepted as a reform but not a goal.

cut-welfare.rationale: Labor legislation and social reform are supported as improving workers' condition; cutting them contradicts the program, although they are not seen as solving the root problem.

worker-ownership.rationale: Orthodox Marxists want social, not enterprise-level, ownership of production by society as a whole; worker ownership of firms is compatible in spirit but not the formula, so agree moderately.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from Kautsky's insistence on democratic rights and free press and the party's experience of anti-socialist laws that surveillance of workers is hostile.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The tradition never addressed drug policy and adherents had no common position; inferred as indifferent.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Orthodox social democrats defended free press and assembly as workers' needs; hate-speech law is not addressed, so a mild lean against restricting speech is inferred.

strong-leader.rationale: Kautsky condemned rule by an elite or single will as undemocratic and counterposed mass democracy; the party stressed collective, majority decision.

state-harmful.rationale: Kautsky says the proletariat must conquer political power and transform the state rather than abolish it overnight; calling it harmful and unnecessary is far from his view.

limit-guns.rationale: No stated position; Marxists historically favored an armed people in principle but gun control as such was not an orthodox question.

empower-police-military.rationale: Kautsky blames capitalist rivalry for militarism that turned Europe into a military camp, so adding to military authority is inferred as disfavored.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Kautsky's text treats prostitution as a product of capitalism that socialism would end; legalization as policy is not addressed, so split.

decide-locally.rationale: Orthodox Marxism favored a centralized democratic republic and centrally conducted socialist production; local autonomy was not a principle.

rehabilitation.rationale: Crime was seen as a product of social conditions to be removed by socialism, implying rehabilitative over punitive approaches; the Erfurt text does not detail prisons.

traditional-family.rationale: Kautsky's commentary treats the family as historically changing form and discusses the 'abolition of the family' charge; he does not hold traditional structures to be foundational.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed in the period (though German social democrats like Bebel and Kautsky opposed anti-homosexual law); inferred mild support from egalitarian principles.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not a primary Second International topic; SPD was increasingly critical of abortion bans, so mild support inferred.

more-religion-public.rationale: Not covered by the sources I opened; inferred from the materialist outlook that religion is a private matter and not a basis for public life.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Orthodox Marxists were internationalist and anti-racist but saw race as secondary to class; active correction is inferred as welcomed but not central.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Kautsky's discussion of the family and woman's position treats sex roles as historically shaped by economic conditions, supporting a social-construction reading.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Kautsky says the proletarian is a citizen of the world and national prejudice fades; preservation of national tradition is not a goal.

gradual-change.rationale: Orthodoxy accepts parliamentary struggle but insists on social revolution replacing the property system; gradual respect for established institutions is rejected as revisionism.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Internationalist solidarity of workers across borders implies opposition to restriction, though Second International debates on immigrant labor were mixed.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Kautsky stresses international solidarity and the International, yet existing bodies of the day were bourgeois; mild inferred support.

free-trade.rationale: Marx-derived orthodoxy supported free trade as accelerating capitalist development without thinking it benefits everyone; adherents split with protectionist views, so neutral.

nation-first.rationale: Kautsky's text holds that proletarians are citizens of the world and the workers of all nations depend on one another.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Orthodox Marxists saw wars as capitalist competition and opposed militarism; military intervention for rights is inferred as distrusted.

open-borders.rationale: The proletarian's lack of a settled country and internationalism point to eventual open borders as an aim, though not a program demand.

limit-growth.rationale: Orthodox Marxism rested on growth of productive forces ripening socialism; limiting growth would contradict this, though ecology was not addressed.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The 19th-century tradition did not address climate; modern adherents would see capitalism as cause and accept state action, inferred.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Productive forces development is the engine of history for orthodox materialism, but social ownership rather than technology alone solves problems; qualified agreement.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic and not tied to principles; adherents would split.

revolution-justified.rationale: Kautsky says the aim is social revolution, conquest of political power by the proletariat, though revolution need not mean violence.

experts-over-public.rationale: Kautsky stresses democracy and mass participation; experts guide but do not override workers, inferred.

central-planning.rationale: Socialist production is conducted by and for society according to plan, replacing market anarchy; Kautsky still expected exchange of surpluses and some trade.

socialized-markets.rationale: Kautsky targets commodity production itself; markets even among social firms would continue the production for sale he wants superseded.

land-value-tax.rationale: Single-tax schemes are reform nostrums that leave capital in place; Kautsky calls most proposed reforms useless or injurious.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inheritance taxes were a standard social-democratic reform, supported as lesser measure while the real aim is abolishing property in means of production.

basic-income.rationale: Not discussed; Kautsky favored work-based distribution in socialism and reform of wages under capitalism, so adherents are split.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Kautsky sees tariffs and militarism as fruits of capitalist rivalry that burden workers; mild opposition inferred.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Socialist production is planned by society, though state-capitalist directing under capitalism is not itself socialism; inferred support.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Kautsky says small production is doomed by economic development and socialism cannot preserve it, though it can help small producers as consumers.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The goal of ending commodity production and wage labor is core, but the sources give no timetable or treatment of money, so agreement is moderate.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Leaving money to the market contradicts replacing commodity production by social production; Kautsky wants social control of credit, not market money.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Kautsky's labor movement is class struggle by independent unions and party against the capitalist class, not state-sanctioned partnership.

one-party-rule.rationale: Kautsky denounces dictatorship as suppressing opposing views and criticizes Soviet exclusion of other socialist parties; he defends democracy and plural socialist parties.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Kautsky stresses universal suffrage and democratic republic as the working class's political terrain; hereditary rule is incompatible.

democracy-best.rationale: Kautsky holds that the proletarian class struggle presupposes democracy and that socialism must extend democracy into the economy.

direct-votes.rationale: The commentary discusses the future state's structure but my extract did not state a view on referendums; adherents like Bebel favored direct legislation yet others stressed parliament.

workers-councils.rationale: Kautsky opposed Soviet-style councils replacing parliament as the basis of power and defended the Commune only as pluralist and democratic.

right-to-secede.rationale: Orthodox socialists affirmed national self-determination in principle while preferring larger states and class unity; they were split.

natural-rulers.rationale: Kautsky rejects rule by an educated elite and sees democracy and mass organization as the foundation.

political-violence-never.rationale: Kautsky treats revolution as a possibility that need not involve violence, but he does not renounce force and condemns pacifist illusions.

war-builds-character.rationale: Kautsky presents militarism as a product of capitalist competition and celebrates May Day protests against war.

separate-church-state.rationale: Not stated in sources opened; inferred from materialist treatment of religion as private and the program's secular outlook.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Orthodoxy rests on materialist science of society, which excludes scripture as basis for law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Orthodox Marxism views the state and law as instruments to be captured by the working class; privatizing them would be capitalist, so rejected.

military-superiority.rationale: Kautsky decries the arms race and militarism; seeking superiority over rivals is inferred as rejected.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The internationalist proletarian is a citizen of the world and national prejudice fades, so ethnic homogeneity is no goal.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Orthodox Marxism treats historical materialism and class struggle as the scientific key to history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Socialist distribution aims at abolishing class distinctions, but Kautsky and the tradition gave work-based distribution first; qualified agreement.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed; adherents would split between anticolonial sympathy and class-first stance.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed; solidarity with colonized peoples is stated but reparations were no Second International demand.

civilizational-union.rationale: Workers' unity across borders is by class, not civilization or religion.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Kautsky says men act in their own interests (not puppets) as a fact, but the socialist ethic is solidarity and collective ownership.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Kautsky defends democratic rights and individual freedom against dictatorship, so rights are not subordinated to duties.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not addressed; materialists regard nature as the arena of human labor, but adherents did not discuss intrinsic value.

limit-population.rationale: Kautsky disputed Malthusian population explanations of poverty, attributing poverty to social institutions; active limiting is disfavored.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Orthodox Marxism views industrial capitalism as progressively developing the productive forces that make socialism possible.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Orthodox determinism held history cannot be hurried and institutions change when conditions mature; adherents welcomed technology but not disruption for its own sake.

human-enhancement.rationale: Anachronistic and not tied to principles.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from emphasis on democratic mass decision-making.

restore-past-order.rationale: Orthodox Marxism is progressive: history moves forward to socialism and small production's past cannot be restored.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Lukács holds orthodoxy is commitment to a method and a total view, rejecting pragmatic eclecticism.

direct-action.rationale: Kautsky urges using universal suffrage and parliament along with union and party organization, not abandoning elections.

means-match-ends.rationale: Kautsky ties democracy as method to socialism's democratic aim, yet orthodoxy also stressed revolutionary conquest; split.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Orthodox Marxism holds that capitalist development of the productive forces is a precondition of socialism, which implies rejecting a return to foraging.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Kautsky discusses socialist production and the division of labor under capitalism; abolition as such is not his view, but classical Marx hinted at it, so mild disagreement.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Kautsky's commentary treats division of products in the future society, but my extract did not specify need; the stage of distribution by need is inferred from the classical goal.

production-for-use.rationale: Kautsky states directly that production for sale must be replaced by socialist production for and by society.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The Erfurt commentary's analysis of wages, profit and the proletariat treats profit as arising from workers' labor unpaid by capital; philanthropy cannot remove this.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Kautsky read the dictatorship of the proletariat as a condition of majority rule, not a form of government suppressing opponents, so he rejects dictatorial power over former rulers.

collective-farming.rationale: Kautsky insists that socialism cannot preserve small farms but would not coerce peasants into collectives; the program emphasizes persuasion.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Kautsky says capitalist competition fuels conflict between nations and militarism, though later he argued ultra-imperialism could avoid wars; hence moderate agreement.

taxation-theft.rationale: Orthodoxy aims at common ownership and conquering the state, treating taxation as normal state function.

harm-principle.rationale: Not addressed; socialists favored restricting property rights beyond harm to others.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Orthodoxy is class-based and treats property rights as historical class instruments; rights belonging only to individuals is rejected, though individual rights are defended against dictatorship.

conscription.rationale: Kautsky critiques militarism; conscription is inferred as opposed except in a people's militia sense.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Kautsky insists on democracy and the vote as the road to power; exit is an irrelevant check.

state-as-business.rationale: The proletariat is to conquer the state and use it for common ownership; running it as a business for customers is the capitalist approach.

positive-liberty.rationale: The commentary on socialism and freedom ties freedom to ending economic dependence of workers on owners.

media-academia-power.rationale: Kautsky stresses class power rooted in property, not universities or media; a free press matters to workers.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Materialist explanation of society by economic conditions rather than race; inferred strong disagreement.

organic-representation.rationale: Kautsky holds that workers should organize in an independent labor party and use universal suffrage in parliament.

total-state.rationale: Kautsky defends democratic rights against dictatorial control of life; the total state is rejected.

national-rebirth.rationale: The movement's aim is class emancipation across nations, not national regeneration.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Kautsky blames capitalist competition for militarism and sees national rivalry as a capitalist contradiction.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Kautsky treats personal bonds of lordship as feudal and socialism as the product of mass democracy, which implies rejecting this.

bound-labor.rationale: Feudal bondage is a pre-capitalist stage of exploitation; socialism aims at free and equal individuals.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Orthodoxy claims historical materialism is a science, though Lukács notes bourgeois ideology shapes thought; the position is that science of society is possible.

universal-morality.rationale: Orthodox materialists held morality historical and class-conditioned while Kautsky's neo-Kantian leanings varied; mild disagreement inferred.

single-common-good.rationale: Class interests are opposed under capitalism, so politics is class struggle rather than a single common good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Kautsky's period preferred assimilation and equal rights in countries of residence; inferred mild opposition.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not addressed; inferred indifferent, with preference for class over national issues.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Kautsky says the decisive question is whether the proletariat can transfer democracy from politics to economics.

school-vouchers.rationale: Not addressed; inferred preference for public education over vouchers.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Not addressed; Kautsky saw crises as inherent to capitalism and not curable by fiscal prudence.

economic-freedom.rationale: Orthodoxy holds economic freedom under capitalism is domination by owners and political freedom rests on democratic action of workers.

rule-by-example.rationale: Kautsky bases politics on democratic mass struggle and law, not rulers' moral example.

national-self-determination.rationale: The Second International recognized national self-determination in principle, though Kautsky's text stresses internationalism.

force-without-un.rationale: Opposition to militarism implies disfavor of unilateral force.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Orthodox Marxism holds itself a scientific method of dialectical materialism; Lukács calls it the road to truth.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Workers of all nations depend on one another, so benefits should not exclude immigrant workers.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not addressed; the workers' movement defended the unemployed (industrial reserve army) as victims of capitalism.

class-collaboration.rationale: Kautsky's account of the class struggle holds the proletariat must rely on its own efforts and dismisses cooperation via philanthropy.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Orthodoxy aims at inheriting culture and science for the working class, not destroying it.

dominated-front.rationale: Not addressed in sources; internationalism is by class rather than state fronts.

workers-nation.rationale: Kautsky says the workers' movement is international in character and the proletarian is a citizen of the world.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The Erfurt tradition demanded women's equality; the commentary treats the dissolution of the proletarian family as a capitalist effect and rejects fixed roles.

ban-interest.rationale: Orthodoxy critiques commodity production and capital as a whole, not interest alone; banning interest on lending is a petty-bourgeois nostrum.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Kautsky's internationalism and the unity of workers across races and nations imply opposition to segregation laws.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Kautsky says the modern state must be conquered by the working class and its economic significance is analyzed as a class instrument.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Internationalism implies solidarity with immigrant workers; assimilation demand is not part of it.

elite-replacement.rationale: Orthodox Marxists explained migration as labour-market movement under capitalism, which leaves no room for a replacement conspiracy.

proportional-representation.rationale: Social democrats pressed for universal suffrage and fair representation, so proportional systems are inferred as supported.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Kautsky's commentary treats women's dependence and the family's dissolution under capitalism, but orthodoxy grounds women's subordination in class and property rather than in patriarchy itself; moderate agreement.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Orthodoxy criticized bourgeois politicians as class representatives, not generic corruption; split.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic coercion contradicts the materialist emphasis on social causes.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Not addressed; consistent with democratic rights emphasis.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The state is to be conquered and used for common ownership of production, far beyond a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The movement's proletarian internationalism and solidarity of workers across nations imply rejecting this; no source addresses mixed marriage.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The commentary pictures socialism as free and equal individuals; classes are to be abolished.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Orthodox thinkers expected socialism to arise from mature capitalism in advanced countries together; Plekhanov-era debates predate the question.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Equality of all citizens before law regardless of creed is inferred, with religion a private matter.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Restrictions on conscience conflict with the democratic freedoms Kautsky demands.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not addressed; religious-based bans contradict secular materialism.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Inferred from treating religion as a private matter.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Kautsky criticized strengthening state power over the democratic base in Russia; orthodoxy expected the state to be transformed, not enhanced.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Kautsky holds that a people is not ripe for socialism while the majority are hostile and the dictatorship of the proletariat means majority rule.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist aims serve capitalist rivalry that the tradition criticizes.

population-transfer.rationale: The movement's internationalism and its defence of persecuted minorities imply opposition to expelling them.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Kautsky does not renounce force in social revolution or the state's coercive capacity; absolute non-aggression is the libertarian position.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Capitalist competition develops the productive forces, but the program replaces competition with planned cooperation.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Kautsky stressed free speech and democracy against suppression; banning parties is inferred as disfavored.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The commentary links freedom to ending workers' dependence on owners, consistent with non-domination.

separated-powers.rationale: Not addressed in sources; parliamentary supremacy was favored by many.

vanguard-party.rationale: Kautsky says socialism was brought to workers by bourgeois intellectuals who broke with their class and joined the party, but he did not demand a disciplined cadre vanguard, so agreement is partial.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The labor movement represents the wage-earning proletariat; the program prioritizes workers' needs, though in class rather than charitable terms.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Not addressed; selling off public housing stock is inferred as against socialization.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Kautsky treats the union movement and strikes as core elements of working-class struggle.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The commentary attributes poverty to capitalist social institutions, not to population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Internationalist solidarity regards national and ethnic differences as fading prejudices.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Kautsky condemned suppression of opposition as dictatorship even by socialists.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Reform measures easing workers' conditions are supported, though Kautsky doubts they remove capitalism's contradictions.

party-controls-media.rationale: Kautsky argued against forcible suppression of the utterance of opponents.

party-commands-army.rationale: Subordinating the state forces to a party contradicts the democratic state Kautsky defended.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Workers' solidarity across borders implies support for easy citizenship.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Kautsky praised the Commune as the work of the whole proletariat; low pay for officials is a Commune measure that orthodox Marxists endorsed, inferred.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Lukács describes the party representing the movement as a whole, and the Social Democrats prided themselves on discipline.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Kautsky later favored a European union and internationalism, but the EU as such is an anachronism; split.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Presidential command over forces conflicts with democratic parliamentary orientation.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not addressed; materialists view church organization as outside politics, with state neutrality.

clerical-rule.rationale: The movement's materialism and demand for democratic socialism imply rejecting rule by clergy.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Kautsky's text opposes war between capitalist states but the Second International mainstream backed national defense in 1914; the revolutionary-defeatist line is Lenin's, so the typical orthodox adherent disagrees.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Orthodox Marxists defended free press and expression as workers' needs.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Presidential term limits were not discussed by Kautsky, who favored parliamentary democracy; adherents have no common stance.

recall-officials.rationale: Kautsky praised the Commune's democracy; recall is inferred as compatible with democratic control.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Not addressed; opposition to militarism suggests support, but orthodox socialists accepted national defense.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Orthodoxy aims at social ownership of means of production, not at making every family a property owner.

people-in-arms.rationale: Kautsky's militarism critique and the tradition's militia ideal lead to inferred support for an armed people.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Kautsky sees small farming doomed and the proletariat as the progressive class; romanticizing rural life is rejected.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The sources never address partitioned nations; class internationalism and self-determination point in different directions.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Kautsky holds that scientific socialism came from educated bourgeois idealists who joined the workers, so he does not disparage the educated.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Orthodox progressivism of stages sat uneasily with relativism; adherents split.

death-penalty.rationale: Socialists opposed capital punishment as a class-justice feature; not addressed directly.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from education reform and women's equality aims.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Kautsky built his social theory on Darwinian evolution and scientific materialism, which implies opposing creationism in schools; intelligent design itself postdates the scope.

minority-language-support.rationale: Internationalism and equal rights imply support for minority languages.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not addressed; split between freedom of conscience and equal law.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill's argument about social conformity is outside the orthodox texts; nothing in Kautsky's defense of democratic freedom settles it.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Solidarity with poorer nations is inferred as favoring cancellation; Kautsky said workers should help backward nations rise.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Marxists regard political forms as resting on the economic basis, so political change without property change is insufficient.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Kautsky defended democratic means and universal suffrage, so an elected assembly is the appropriate means.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Kautsky holds democracy a precondition of the proletarian struggle and defended political freedoms; temporary restriction for development is inferred as rejected.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Kautsky says workers should help backward nations rise; inferred support for solidarity-based aid.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from opposition to militarism and arms races.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Not addressed; adherents would split between parliamentary supremacy and direct election.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Not addressed; inferred that bankers' autonomy from elected control serves capital.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Class internationalism rejects historic-homeland claims; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Orthodoxy holds private property in means of production is a historical form to be superseded by social ownership, closer to this than to absolute property rights.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Wikipedia notes that anti-revisionists call the Soviet and Chinese states state capitalist while others differ; Kautsky condemned Bolshevik rule but orthodox adherents are split.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Not addressed in the period; no stable position.

collective-defense.rationale: Not addressed; Second International stressed national defense but opposed militarist blocs.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Opposition to annexation is inferred from the movement's commitment to self-determination and anti-militarism.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; split between separation and curbing.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Kautsky's democratic republic gives no stated view on a symbolic head of state; adherents would split.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Opposition to militarism and support for self-determination imply reluctance, though not a stated position.

region-keeps-system.rationale: One-country-two-systems arrangements are unaddressed; orthodoxy neither forbids regional autonomy nor endorses a separate economic system.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The movement's materialism and republican democratic programme imply rejecting a sacred head of state.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Progressive taxation was a standard social-democratic reform; a flat rate favors the wealthy.

character-from-environment.rationale: Kautsky's treatment of the proletarian and capitalist classes holds that men's actions follow their social conditions.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Kautsky's defence of democracy and the rule of law against dictatorship implies rejecting a ruler above the law.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Orthodoxy favors rule by the many through democracy, not mixed regimes.

leader-cult.rationale: Kautsky contrasts democratic mass movement with dictatorship; leader cults are inferred as alien.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody presumptions are a modern family-law question the Erfurt commentary never touches, so adherents are split.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Orthodoxy expected classes to disappear with socialism; the thesis that the struggle intensifies is Stalinist and Maoist.

land-redistribution.rationale: Kautsky says small farming cannot be preserved by socialism, hence transfer of land to small cultivators is not the orthodox program; split.

refugee-return.rationale: Support for return is inferred from solidarity and equal rights.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The Erfurt Programme's demand that religion be a private matter implies opposing any legal penalty for leaving a religion.

women-must-cover.rationale: Orthodox socialists supported women's equality; compulsory dress is rejected.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Unity is by class, not ancestry.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Austro-Marxists proposed it while Kautsky and others disagreed; split.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Orthodox socialists favored minorities' struggle for equal rights alongside the working class in their countries.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Wikipedia identifies historical materialism, with changing economic conditions as history's driver, as orthodoxy's core.

ban-cartels.rationale: Kautsky treats syndicates and trusts as stages in the growth of large production leading toward socialization, not something to break up.

no-bailouts.rationale: Not addressed; reformist support for workers versus not propping up capital.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Not addressed; supports majority rule but no stated view on courts.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred from commitment to women's equality; quotas were not an orthodox demand.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarkic imperial blocs are products of capitalist rivalry and contradict internationalism.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: International labor standards fit internationalist labor legislation aims.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Wikipedia describes orthodoxy as deterministic: history cannot be hurried and revolution waits for ripe economic conditions.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Abolition of class privilege is core and the democratic program opposes hereditary rule.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Kautsky wants workers to help backward nations rise, not rule them.

patriotic-education.rationale: The proletarian is a citizen of the world and national prejudice fades.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Orthodoxy treated race as secondary to class, so it gives no clear answer on admissions preferences.

public-money-creation.rationale: Social control of credit follows from social ownership; Kautsky discusses commerce and credit as part of capitalism to be socialized.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Orthodoxy held capitalism would collapse through internal contradictions and denounced Bernstein for denying it.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Imperial ambition is a capitalist feature.

delink-world-market.rationale: Orthodoxy saw capitalist world-market development as progressive; delinking is inferred as rejected.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Kautsky criticizes craft aristocracy of labor but sees workers as exploited; the imperialist-profit version is Leninist.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Inferred from equality and worker solidarity.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Kautsky defends democratic rights but the sources say nothing on entrenching them against majorities.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Orthodox socialists opposed colonial rule but had no doctrine on treaty validity; adherents would split.

elective-rulers.rationale: Kautsky insists on democracy and universal suffrage as the means to power.

minority-veto.rationale: Majority rule is central to Kautsky's democratic view.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Not directly addressed; inferred from revolutionary right of the proletariat.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Kautsky urges workers to use parliament and expects it to be transformed by proletarian participation.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics was never part of Second International orthodoxy; no stated position.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use for food or research was outside orthodox concerns, so no stated position.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Kautsky dismisses philanthropy as limited and says the proletariat must rely on itself.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Kautsky holds that every class struggle is political.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Frankfurt School theme rather than orthodox; Wikipedia places it among later Western Marxism.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Hegemony is Gramscian Western Marxism, not orthodox; orthodoxy stresses economic and state power.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory is later; orthodoxy located exploitation chiefly within class relations.

party-own-road.rationale: Social democratic parties were national bodies in an International; Kautsky's own road for Germany is inferred.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Workers' solidarity favors help for backward nations.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Rule by one descent group over another cuts against the equal democratic citizenship Kautsky assumes, inferred as mildly opposed.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Anachronistic for the Second International era; modern adherents would likely agree.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Kautsky condemned Bolshevik dictatorship but orthodoxy never framed it as equivalence with fascism; split.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred from materialist reading that slavery's economic basis drove the conflict.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Monuments debates are modern and unaddressed; adherents would split between historical memory and rejecting honors for exploiters.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not a Second International theme; orthodox adherents would likely tie disadvantage to class and give no firm answer.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: The tradition never discussed this question, so no position can be stated.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Orthodoxy treats stages of development as universal rather than civilizational.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Kautsky criticizes militarism and expects democratic politics.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred from treating household labor as productive work and the dissolution of the family under capitalism.

filial-duty.rationale: The Erfurt commentary describes the changing, dissolving proletarian family but does not rule on duties of grown children.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Nationalist protectionism is not an orthodox aim.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from women's equality and treatment of family as historically changing.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Kautsky praises the Commune as a democratic proletarian regime; delegates bound and removable follow from it.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Individual market accounts contradict social provision and collective ownership.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Kautsky favors social ownership of production but his sources opened do not address use-based land tenure for individuals.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from internationalism and opposition to private land.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Not addressed; adherents would stress class.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Consumerism critique is a later theme; orthodox adherents emphasized production relations and have no stated view.

corporate-influence.rationale: The state as class instrument and capital's power over politics.

residents-only-property.rationale: Restrictions by locality sit badly with workers' solidarity and free movement, inferred as mildly opposed.

job-guarantee.rationale: Industrial reserve army is a capitalist feature; job guarantee inferred as welcome reform.

democratic-peace.rationale: Orthodoxy saw wars as capitalist rivalry regardless of regime form.

industrial-unions.rationale: Kautsky criticizes craft separation as aristocracy of labor and expects its erosion.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The movement's materialist class analysis and its opposition to antisemitism as a diversion from class politics imply rejecting minority conspiracy theories.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Kautsky discusses the so-called abolition of the family as a charge, but the sources do not favor ending legal marriage.

local-production.rationale: Inferred; socialist production plans at society level.

informal-organisation.rationale: Kautsky says a secret organisation cannot be democratic and urges a mass party.

religious-nation.rationale: The movement's internationalism and treatment of religion as a private matter imply rejecting a nation defined by religion.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Kautsky distinguishes private property in instruments of production from other property.

defeat-communism.rationale: Kautsky attacked Bolshevik dictatorship in 1918 and later backed its democratic overthrow, but the movement's own goal was a socialist, communist society, so a call to defeat communism fits it only for the Bolshevik regime.

religion-illusion.rationale: Materialist outlook treats religion as ideological reflection of conditions; extent not sourced precisely.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Orthodoxy holds capitalism develops productive forces and prepares socialism.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Kautsky's discussion of proletarian family and woman's lot in capitalism ties women's condition to economics.

socialized-care.rationale: Bebel argued for it but Kautsky text does not.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Linguistic purism is nationalist in spirit and conflicts with the cosmopolitan outlook Kautsky describes, inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with internal nations are not addressed by orthodox sources, so no position.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Kautsky regards small cooperative utopian communities as utopian socialism, replaced by scientific socialism.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Orthodoxy holds socialism to be the only alternative.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The question is anachronistic for a scope ending around 1918; denial is assumed to conflict with the movement's materialist method.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: German Social Democrats opposed Paragraph 175; inferred.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Kautsky argues dictatorship suppresses opponents' utterance and democracy requires free debate.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Kautsky traces militarism to imperial competition and wants workers to help backward nations rise, not be governed for a metropole's gain.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Religious obligation to war contradicts materialism.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Orthodoxy's materialist science of society offers no basis for religious legitimacy and Kautsky's democratic path excludes armed removal of rulers on religious grounds.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Kautsky says the decisive question is transferring democracy from politics to economics.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Wikipedia says orthodoxy treated race as secondary; intersectionality is later.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: An anachronistic issue for the Second International; no stated position.

assisted-dying.rationale: Medical ethics lay outside orthodox Marxism's concerns, so no stated position.

alienated-labor.rationale: Alienation emphasized by Western Marxism; orthodox Kautskyan texts focus on exploitation.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The movement grounds political authority in the democratic mass of working people, which implies rejecting divine authority.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Orthodoxy treated religion as private but did not address dress rules in state institutions.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred mild support: the workers' movement backed labor legislation against employer abuses, though this specific issue is modern.

social-market-economy.rationale: Kautsky says reforms preserving private property are inoperative in resolving contradictions.

rich-first.rationale: Orthodoxy aims at common ownership and equal conditions for the working class rather than letting some grow rich first, inferred from the socialist program.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The movement's demand for a democratic republic implies rejecting hereditary succession of leaders.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred from solidarity with weaker nations and opposition to imposing capitalist burdens on workers; the issue is modern.

property-franchise.rationale: Kautsky calls universal ballot a prerequisite of a healthy proletarian movement.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Orthodox Marxism traced women's subordination to property relations but treated mastery of nature as progress; inferred.

reification.rationale: Commodity fetishism is part of Marx's Capital which orthodoxy upholds, and Lukacs's essay on orthodoxy builds on it; Kautsky himself used it little.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Kautsky's political-struggle writing sees the bourgeois press as a class weapon, though he defended democratic freedoms as real and worth winning; inferred.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Kautsky defended democracy and law against Bolshevik dictatorship and arbitrary rule by decree.

racial-franchise.rationale: The strand fought for universal suffrage and internationalism and denied that race divides workers.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; the strand favoured mass parliamentary and party participation, and no position on the medium can be drawn.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from Kautsky's case that open democracy is the precondition of working-class struggle.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Inferred from the Social Democratic view that religion is a private matter and from its universalism.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred from its internationalism and view that such prejudice divides the working class.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Politics ran through the mass party and parliament; sortition is inferred to be alien to it.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Religion was treated as a private matter outside the program, so no stand on doctrinal reform is inferred.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Kautsky's Erfurt commentary describes capital concentrating in few hands and the propertied class dominating state and society; a Marxist reads this as domination of workers, though 'free society' is not the framing used.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Not a Second International topic; inferred from the Erfurt Program's demand for equal civil rights without distinction of sex or status.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Orthodox Marxism treats religion as a private matter (Erfurt Program) and expects it to fade with class society, so adherents were split on state promotion; inferred.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred: the orthodox view sees the state as a class instrument to be captured and used, and the sources propose no abolition of police or prisons before socialism.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred: orthodox Marxism favors majority rule through universal suffrage and parliament, not consociational power-sharing among communities.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The Erfurt Program rejects charity as a substitute for ending the proletariat's dependence and demands public social legislation and abolition of private ownership of production.

term-limits.rationale: Inferred: the mass party seeks sustained parliamentary majorities and has no stated stance on term limits; limits cut against professional party representation.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred: delegation to trusted individuals runs against the disciplined party and parliamentary route; the sources never address it.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Inferred: orthodox Marxism's focus is class struggle and the collapse of capitalism, so extinction risk would not be a top policy priority.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from the Erfurt Program's demand for full equality of women and men; religious offices are not discussed.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from the Erfurt Program's demand for equality of the sexes in law, including family law.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from the Second International's internationalism and demand for universal suffrage, though local voting for non-citizens was not discussed.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from Erfurt-style social democracy's support for reforms easing workers' conditions; rent caps were not a stated item.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred: orthodoxy aimed to socialise the means of production, not to abolish patent or copyright law, which it did not address.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from Kautsky's democratic, anti-militarist social democracy, which organised youth in voluntary workers' associations.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from the Second International's anti-militarism; nuclear weapons postdate the doctrine.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from the Second International's anti-militarist and internationalist position; no direct treatment of bases.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred from its democratic, humanitarian commitments; the doctrine did not address official recognition of genocide.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Kautsky's account of surplus value treats rent, interest and profit as unearned appropriation of workers' labour, a core part of the orthodox analysis.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred: Kautsky accepted that workers may use force in defence, and orthodoxy was never pacifist.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred from its class-based historical materialism, which explains history by modes of production rather than national continuity.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred: orthodoxy treated sex as a biological fact and women's emancipation as a result of economic change; the constructivist thesis is anachronistic.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred: orthodoxy saw women's emancipation as part of the single proletarian class movement, not as a separate identity politics.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from its scientific, secular outlook, which does not hallow national sacrifice.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Orthodox Marxism treats politics as class struggle grounded in material interests under historical materialism, not as a spiritual contest.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred: the Second International was internationalist and did not address diaspora-homeland questions.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred from materialism, which holds that the economic base and political power shape culture, not the reverse.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred: religion was a private matter in the Erfurt programme and the doctrine did not address religious language.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred: orthodoxy treated religion as a private matter and did not set tests for religious texts.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred from Second International internationalism and its view that class, not nation, divides economic life.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine is internationalist and did not seek ethnically defined regions.

independent-unions.rationale: Kautsky treated unions as one arm of the class struggle alongside the party, separate from the state, though tied to the party in practice.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Kautsky defines the proletarian dictatorship as rule by the majority class through democracy, and criticised Bolshevik rule by a party elite.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The Erfurt programme sought social ownership of production; extension to local public services is inferred.

second-chamber.rationale: Social democrats attacked upper houses as bulwarks of privilege and favoured a parliament elected by universal suffrage; inferred.

municipal-property.rationale: Kautsky's commonwealth envisioned society-wide ownership organised nationally rather than by localities.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The orthodox model was a centralised mass party and national parliament, not local assemblies; inferred.

family-wage.rationale: The labour movement of the period sought wages enough to live on for workers' households; inferred.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Anachronistic; nothing in the sources bears on drug regulation.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: The orthodox faith in science and progress favours such public research; inferred, as it was never discussed.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Anachronistic; no source gives grounds either way.

online-anonymity.rationale: Kautsky defended freedom of press and association against suppression (s6); extension to pseudonymous speech is inferred.

person-over-state.rationale: Kautsky's insistence on democracy and criticism of Bolshevik suppression of opposition implies that individuals are not mere means; inferred.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Orthodox Marxism rests on dialectical-materialist method and historical materialism as science.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: No stated position on the constitution of regions; inferred neutral.

gm-crops.rationale: Faith in the progressive development of productive forces suggests support for technology in agriculture; inferred.

dense-cities.rationale: Anachronistic; no source speaks to the environmental effect of density.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Kautsky's Erfurt commentary puts class struggle and internationalism above any other group division.

racial-pride.rationale: Internationalism and the class framework leave no room for pride in race or ancestry as a political value; inferred.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Kautsky's commentary attacks militarism and the Second International accepted only defensive wars.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Inferred from the class-first internationalism of the Second International; Kautsky did write on nationality but I did not open a source on it, so this is an inference.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from Kautsky's insistence on universal suffrage and one proletarian party uniting workers regardless of creed, which excludes separate religious electorates.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred: orthodoxy explained international conflict through capitalist rivalry and militarism rather than plots to dismantle nations.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred from the Erfurt-era social-democratic demand for free public education; the sources open here do not list tuition specifically.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred: orthodoxy sought socialised production for use, not market pricing of externalities, which would leave private ownership in place.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from the progressive outlook of historical materialism and socialism as a better order for later generations; not discussed directly.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred: Kautsky and the SPD sought women's equality through the class struggle and treated sex-based political values as non-class distinctions.

arms-reduction.rationale: The Erfurt commentary opposes militarism and standing armies in favour of a people's militia, so reducing armaments is inferred.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from the Social Democratic demand for democratic control of foreign policy against secret cabinet diplomacy; not found in the opened sources.

capital-controls.rationale: Orthodoxy aimed at abolishing private ownership outright instead of regulating capital flows, so adherents would not endorse nor firmly oppose this reform.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Kautsky's writings treat armed force mainly as an instrument of class rule and mass militias were a Second International idea; nothing in the sources settles whether non-state armed groups should be disarmed.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Second International orthodoxy opposed militarism and war between states but through the party and international working-class action, not individual refusal; inferred from Kautsky's discussion of militarism.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Kautsky's Erfurt Program commentary makes trade unions and collective struggle over wages and hours a core part of the workers' fight.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Tax credits are an anachronistic device; Erfurt-style reform supported labor legislation but held that reforms leaving private ownership intact cannot remove capitalism's contradictions, so adherents would be split.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the view that capitalist states serve the ruling class and that bourgeois fiscal discipline falls on workers, though Kautsky did not address borrowing limits.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred from the Second International's internationalism and anti-imperialism; developing-country policy was not a pre-1914 program item.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Kautsky's Dictatorship of the Proletariat argues that the proletariat should win the existing democratic state through universal suffrage and parliament, and he rejected the Bolshevik destruction of democratic institutions.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Orthodoxy holds that socialism needs one planned, socially owned mode of production (production for use), so a fixed system is expected rather than free experiment.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Anachronistic; Marxist value theory treats labor as the source of value and the economic pricing of nature was not discussed, so inferred opposition.

sacred-nation.rationale: Orthodox Marxism is materialist and treats the nation as a historical class-bound formation, with the working class internationalist, so a sacred nation is rejected.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from its support for social reform that eases workers' lot; student loans are anachronistic.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Anachronistic; orthodoxy analysed class relations rather than regional exploitation, and Kautsky did not apply colonial analogies inside states.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Orthodox Marxism treated human nature as historically formed by modes of production, not a fixed basis for rights; inferred from its historical materialism.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from Kautsky's emphasis on a free press and democratic freedoms as conditions of the workers' struggle, though public broadcasting is anachronistic.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Inferred from Marxist materialism, which treats religion as a product of social conditions rather than a shared spiritual truth; the sources do not discuss comparative religion.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred: Kautsky's agrarian writing held that small peasants were being squeezed by capital, but orthodoxy was divided on whether to support them with state price guarantees; the sources here do not settle it.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Second International antimilitarism and the aim of disarmament, though orthodoxy would not favour unilateral disarmament by a workers' state surrounded by rivals either, so the disagreement is mild.

workers-own-party.rationale: Orthodox Marxism centred on an independent mass workers' party, as the SPD was, that fights the class struggle apart from bourgeois parties.

ban-fgm.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the Erfurt Program's demand for equality of the sexes before the law and Marxist hostility to oppressive custom.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred: the Erfurt Program called for the legal equality of women with men, which extends to property and inheritance rights.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Inferred: Second International Marxists were internationalist and did not treat language names as grounds for division, but the sources do not address the question.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred: orthodoxy favoured social legislation and public regulation by the state over reliance on private lawsuits, and would see tort suits as a bourgeois remedy.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred: orthodox Marxism looked to universal suffrage and parliament, and regarded traditional authority as a pre-capitalist survival, so a formal role for chiefs conflicts with it.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Anachronistic; orthodoxy believed in developing the productive forces and gave no ecological priority, yet it did not prize individual liberty over collective ends; inferred as genuinely split.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred: orthodoxy treated crime as a product of social conditions and favoured reform over harsh fixed punishment; the sources do not discuss sentencing.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Anachronistic; orthodoxy was internationalist, with no documented position on language requirements, and adherents could go either way.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Kautsky saw unions as organs of class struggle that need broad membership; inferred that compulsion to join is acceptable, so a right-to-work rule is opposed.

voter-id.rationale: The Second International fought for universal, easily exercised suffrage; inferred opposition to added barriers.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The Erfurt Program demanded that religion be declared a private matter and the church separated from the state, which rules out legal precedence for any interpretation.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Kautsky held democracy to be the rule of the majority and the ground of proletarian struggle, but treated it as tied to class content, not merely to elections.

premarital-sex.rationale: Orthodox Marxists, following Engels and Bebel, criticised bourgeois marriage and favoured women's freedom in sexual relations; inferred.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Anachronistic; the SPD's defence of free press and assembly implies opposition to state cutoffs; inferred.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Anachronistic; the orthodoxy wanted social reform through public provision and socialisation of production, not a market-style cash transfer; inferred.

women-suffrage.rationale: The Erfurt Program demanded universal, equal suffrage without distinction of sex, and the SPD championed women's voting rights.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Orthodoxy traced women's subjection mainly to property relations and the family under private ownership, with religion secondary; adherents are split.

race-social-construct.rationale: Orthodoxy opposed racial theories as ideology serving the ruling class, though biological language was common in its era; inferred.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement wanted legal equality but had no notion of dedicated state agencies; neutral.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Kautsky's commonwealth abolishes private ownership of the means of production, and first-claim title to resources runs against that.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Second International orthodoxy predates international criminal courts; inferred only loosely and the sources do not discuss them.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Orthodox Marxism treats historical materialism as science and religion as a private matter in the Erfurt programme, so inerrant scripture is rejected.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Not addressed for self-rule; inferred from the Erfurt programme's demand for equal rights of women and men.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Anachronistic: Kautsky condemned Bolshevik dictatorship (s5) yet favoured socialised property, so he would defend the economic base only conditionally.

indirect-election.rationale: Kautsky stressed universal suffrage and parliamentary democracy (s5), which implies direct election; he did not discuss delegate systems.

national-church-status.rationale: The Erfurt programme demands that religion be declared a private matter and the separation of church and state.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Second International Marxists were split on national autonomy; the sources do not discuss it.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Second International views on self-determination were mixed.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; anachronistic for the pre-1914 orthodoxy.

simple-living.rationale: Orthodoxy expected socialism to grow out of industrial abundance, not austerity; inferred from its view of capitalist development.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred views would be mixed.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from the Erfurt programme's equality of the sexes and its preference for a people's militia over a standing army.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Inferred from the Erfurt commentary's class-first internationalism: the nation is not treated as a spiritual unit, and workers' solidarity cuts across it.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Kautsky insisted on democracy and legality and condemned Bolshevik terror, so killing suspects without trial would be incompatible with his position.

close-ties-china.rationale: The Second International orthodoxy predates modern China and ties to great powers were not a program question; no position can be inferred.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred from Kautsky's internationalism, which opposes nationalist state projects on behalf of co-ethnics abroad.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Kautsky's program abolishes private ownership of the means of production, land included, in favour of social ownership, which implies society's claim on natural resources.

self-ownership.rationale: Inferred: orthodoxy treats the worker's formal ownership of labour-power as the basis of wage exploitation and favours social planning over absolute individual rights.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Inferred from the Erfurt-era demand for progressive taxation falling on property rather than on workers' daily purchases; the sources do not discuss sales taxes.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Inferred from the social-democratic preference for universal provision and labour legislation rather than means-tested relief of the poor.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Kautsky makes the mass party, trade unions and parliament the instruments of the working class, so a leader bypassing them is contrary to his strategy.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred from the orthodox view that the capitalist state serves propertied interests, which it opposes; no program item is about special privileges for firms.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Inferred from the Second International demand that religion be a private matter and politics be organised by class, not confession.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Inferred from orthodoxy's faith in progressive development of productive forces; reviving ancestral values has no place in its historical materialism.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred from the Erfurt-era commitment to equal rights for women; divorce law is not discussed in the sources.

national-resource-control.rationale: Inferred: orthodoxy wants natural wealth under social ownership, though it frames this as class rather than national control.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Kautsky's critique holds that voluntary wage contracts under private ownership still produce exploitation, so a fair process does not justify the outcome.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Kautsky regarded reforms leaving ownership intact as unable to remove capitalism's contradictions yet supported reforms in practice; no view on this tax can be inferred.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Orthodoxy treated class as the decisive division and rarely discussed race; the statement is anachronistic and adherents could read it either way.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Inferred from Kautsky's insistence on democratic legality and majority rule over extra-legal claims, though he saw law as class-shaped.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred from Kautsky's expectation that technical progress shortens the working day and eases labour under socialism.

multipolar-world.rationale: Inferred from Kautsky's internationalism and opposition to militarism, which favour international working-class solidarity over rival power blocs.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: The labour theory of value is part of the Marxist economics Kautsky systematised and which orthodoxy defended against revisionist critics.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Kautsky was internationalist but the pre-1914 SPD also mixed defence of the homeland with class politics; the sources do not settle it.

material-over-identity.rationale: Inferred from orthodoxy's concentration on class struggle and economic interests as the driver of politics.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Kautsky's commonwealth replaces commodity production with production for use, and he opposed single-party dictatorship, so both halves of the statement conflict with his view.

missingStatements.text: Capitalism will collapse through its own internal contradictions.
missingStatements.rationale: Collapse theory is the orthodox doctrine that Kautsky held and Bernstein's revisionism denied.

missingStatements.text: Socialism cannot be reached before capitalism has developed the economic conditions for it.
missingStatements.rationale: Plekhanov and the Mensheviks argued Russia had to pass through a capitalist stage, and orthodoxy held history cannot be hurried.

missingStatements.text: Socialists should use universal suffrage and parliament to win political power for the working class.
missingStatements.rationale: Kautsky calls the universal ballot a prerequisite of a healthy proletarian movement and urges workers to use parliament.

missingStatements.text: Reforms that leave private ownership of the means of production in place cannot remove capitalism's contradictions.
missingStatements.rationale: Kautsky pronounces such reforms inoperative against the growing contradictions, and orthodoxy attacked Bernstein's reformism.

notes: Kautsky's line is contested within the tradition: Lukacs makes orthodoxy a matter of method rather than theses, Leninists claimed the mantle while rejecting Kautsky, and impossibilists reject reformism. Answers follow Kautsky's mainstream Second International position.
